Package hadur2.core.physics

package hadur2.core.physics
The engine's physics and the geometry built on it: the bottom layer that the duel's gun, surf, waves and energy ledger, and the melee brain, all stand on.
  • Rules and Angles: Robocode's game rules and angle normalisation, copied so the core need not import the engine (CORE-1) and checked bit for bit against it by PhysicsMatchesEngineProperties.
  • BattleField: the field's walls as a robot's centre sees them (18 px in from the edges), the wall-distance features and wall smoothing.
  • MovementPredictor: tick-by-tick prediction under the engine's turn, acceleration and braking rules, and the precise maximum escape angle that waves scale their guess factors by and the surf takes its destinations from.
  • DiaUtils: small shared helpers (projection, bearings, bullet flight times, firing-angle grids, back-as-front driving).

Conventions throughout: positions in px with the origin at the field's bottom-left and +y north; angles in radians with 0 north, growing clockwise (so x uses sin and y uses cos); velocities in px/tick, negative when reversing; time in ticks. The one exception is Rules' turn-rate constants, which are the engine's degrees per tick. An orbit direction of +1 is clockwise round the point orbited.

Dependencies, enforced by ArchitectureTest: like the whole core, nothing here may use robocode.* (CORE-1), any JDK package beyond java.lang, java.util and java.awt.geom, randomness, threads, reflection, I/O or a clock (RES-6), or a mutable static field (CORE-2). This package may use the model, but never the gun, movement, KNN, replay, opponent-memory, melee or posture packages, or the adapt and policy packages; those all depend on it instead. The energy ledger may depend on this package and nothing else in the core, so that only the engine's rules decide which energy drops become waves (WAVE-1). The package is one of the duel's, pinned by DuelIdentityTest.

  • Classes
    Class
    Description
    Angles
    Angle normalisation, bit-for-bit identical to robocode.util.Utils so the core behaves exactly as it did when it called the engine's helpers.
    BattleField
    The battle field's walls, as seen by a robot's centre, and the geometry that depends on them: clamping a point into the field, how far a target can move before a wall stops it (two of the gun's and the surf's KNN features), and wall smoothing.
    DiaUtils
    Small geometry and arithmetic helpers shared by the whole core: projecting points, bearings between points, bullet flight times, the orbit's acceleration sign, firing-angle grids and a Wald margin of error.
    MovementPredictor
    Tick-by-tick prediction of a robot's movement under Robocode's physics, and the precise maximum escape angle built on it.
    Rules
    The Robocode game rules the core relies on, identical to robocode.Rules.
